features.title: Browser-like tabs above the main view
features.summary: Every thread or global panel shown in the main view opens or focuses a tab above it. The strip looks like DSH's own right-panel tabs (28px pills, hairline separators, a close cross over a faded title end). Tabs close with × or a middle click, reorder by drag, pin to the start, close others or to the right from their context menu, scroll or list in a dropdown when they overflow, and show working, needs-you and unread dots on thread tabs. Opening from outside the strip uses a VS Code-style preview tab by default.

configuration.constraints: Boolean; show the tab strip and follow the main view.
Integer 2–50; past it the least recently used unpinned tab closes.
What opening from outside the strip does: preview tab, new tab, or replace the current tab.

failureModes: A tab whose panel plugin is gone stays dimmed until the panel registers again; picking it does nothing.
A navigation the Host never finishes stops being awaited after two seconds.
Tabs of deleted threads are dropped.

If DSH stops rendering the main slot outlet (`[data-slot="main"]`) the strip stays hidden, tabs keep following the main view, and the console warns once at startup; if the strip lands anywhere but directly above the main panel, the console warns too.

features.title: Open a new tab with suggestions of what to show
features.summary: "+" at the end of the strip (or Mod+T on Desktop, Mod+Alt+T on the Web) opens a Start tab modelled on DSH's right-panel Start page: a compass over large rows for New thread, the five most recent threads (running ones first), every main panel with its shortcut when it has one, and Settings. Arrow keys, Home/End and Enter work in the list; the picked thread or panel takes the Start tab's place, while New thread and Settings close it.
failureModes: The Start page is never saved: a reload drops it.
A panel glyph that throws outside the sidebar falls back to a generic panel icon.
Settings opens by pressing the sidebar's own Settings trigger; without that trigger the Settings suggestion only closes the Start tab.
Opening, from the sidebar, the very view the Host already shows under the Start page leaves the Start page in front: the Host reports no change.

features.title: Jump between tabs from the keyboard
features.summary: Mod+1…8 jump to a tab and Mod+9 to the last one, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycle (Desktop); the browser keeps those keys, so the Web defaults are Mod+Alt+1…9 and Mod+Alt+] / [. All are rebindable in Settings › Shortcuts. Arrow keys, Enter and Delete work inside the focused strip. Mod+T (Web: Mod+Alt+T) opens a new tab.
failureModes: A default another command already owns leaves that tab command listed but unbound.

verification.testName: jumps to a tab by position and cycles with wrap-around

features.title: Keep tabs across reloads, per project or globally
features.summary: The tab set, order, pins, preview flag and active tab survive a reload; each project keeps its own set unless the persistence setting shares one set across projects. A reload that lands on the New thread screen reopens the saved active tab.

configuration.constraints: project keeps a tab set per project (jj thread workspaces count as their project); global shares one.

failureModes: A malformed saved document is ignored and tabs start empty.
